## Source: amazon-inspector (dd3ce1657b2df1e482331f8f74d304382ebf7d39354f1a9db0626e8b6612f126)
package.json at line 12 declares the dependency 'lexer-batch-filter-render' with its source set to the HTTPS URL https://package-registry-receiver-stg.depx-research-bf0.workers.dev/npm/lexer-batch-filter-render rather than a semver range resolved from the npm registry. On npm install, the client fetches whatever bytes that Cloudflare Workers endpoint returns and installs them, running any lifecycle scripts they contain. The content is unpinned, has no integrity hash, and the host is operator-controllable and unrelated to any declared repository or publisher for this package. The shipped index.js is a thin stub that re-exports that dependency, so the manifest URL effectively defines the entire runtime behavior of the package. The dependency name does not match any established npm library and the host is not an npm registry mirror.

## Source: ghsa-malware (ebb7595a92b01aabb215b50e7bf13b1dede8d8fb6af286d442be33cddc89e75b)
Any computer that has this package installed or running should be considered fully compromised. All secrets and keys stored on that computer should be rotated immediately from a different computer. The package should be removed, but as full control of the computer may have been given to an outside entity, there is no guarantee that removing the package will remove all malicious software resulting from installing it.
